idiom_name: const pipeline = [parse, validate, enrich]; value = pipeline.reduce(...)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no pipe operator - the TC39 pipeline proposal is still a proposal - so the pipeline is a named array of stage functions driven by reduce or a small pipe helper: each stage is an ordinary unary function and the array is the ordered, inspectable stage list that replaces the classic Pipeline class. This is the default for in-memory values; Node's stream.pipeline is the library realization when the payload is a stream.
code_sketch:
const stages = [parseJson, validate, enrich];
const result = stages.reduce((value, stage) => stage(value), input);
pitfalls: Array helpers passed directly as stages receive (value, index, array), so functions such as parseInt or a stage that inspects its second argument must be wrapped.
Async stages inside reduce silently return promises; sequential awaiting requires a for-of loop or a dedicated helper, not reduce.
Stages that close over mutable module state share it across every run; a pipeline that is built once and reused captures the first configuration.

variants.name: Node.js stream.pipeline with backpressure
variants.implementation_notes: Node's stream module provides the named pipeline: `stream.pipeline(source, ...transforms, destination)` composes streams, propagates errors by destroying the chain, and with the promises API returns a promise that settles when the destination finishes; an AbortSignal in the options cancels the whole pipeline (Node docs). Streams carry data chunk by chunk with built-in backpressure, so this is the realization for files, sockets and other I/O; keep the stage array for in-memory values.
pitfalls: The callback pipeline from 'node:stream' and the promise one from 'node:stream/promises' are different entry points; mixing them loses cancellation and error aggregation.
A transform implemented as an async generator must honour the signal passed to it, or the pipeline never completes when the source is aborted.
Object-mode and Buffer-mode streams mismatch at run time rather than at composition time, so a stage that expected strings can silently receive Buffers.
